title: Learning Interpretable Options by Identifying Reward Diffusion Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning
claim: A familiar physical analogy, a single-source single-sink network of resistors, grounds the abstract quantity the method builds on.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, source and sink arrows at the ends
description: A black-and-white circuit diagram drawn at a slight diagonal. Two square resistor loops sit at the left and right ends and are joined by a single series resistor in the middle. Dark navy dots mark the nodes. A bold red arrow labelled I_in enters the left loop at the source node s. A blue arrow labelled I_out leaves the right loop at the sink node g. A middle node is labelled i. The eye goes first to the red and blue arrows, then along the zigzag resistors. Because all current must pass through the central chain, the chain is the bottleneck. This is the electrical analogue of reward flowing through an MDP. The figure has no legend, no equations and no panels.
caption: Single-source single-sink resistance network
abstract: Bottleneck states, which connect distinct regions of the state space, provide a principled and interpretable basis for constructing temporal abstractions in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL). However, existing bottleneck identification methods primarily rely on topological analysis of the state-transition graph, limiting their scalability to high-dimensional or continuous domains. To address this challenge, we introduce Value Power Strength (VPS), a value function-based metric inspired by the analogy between the Bellman equation and Kirchhoff’s current law, to quantify bottleneck property via the diffusion of reward in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). VPS is estimated efficiently using value functions learned from random reward signals and captures reward diffusion bottlenecks in both discrete and continuous state spaces. Leveraging VPS, we design options that guide agents toward or away from bottleneck regions. Experimental results on classic tabular domains, continuous-control PointMaze, and Atari 2600 games demonstrate that the VPS-based framework discovers semantically meaningful subgoals and substantially improves exploration efficiency.
